title: Value embeddings on every layer (FLOP-free capacity)
description: has_ve() now returns True for all layers, so value_embeds goes from 6 tables to 12 (25.2M -> 50.3M params, 71.3M -> 96.5M total); FLOPs/token unchanged at 3.46e8; nothing else touched.
reflection: NEGATIVE: val_bpb 0.987643 vs baseline 0.986277, i.e. +0.0014 worse, about 1.5x the ~0.0009 noise floor. The throughput half of my prediction was right and the capacity half was wrong. Cost was cheap exactly as forecast: FLOPs/token identical (3.46e8), total_tokens 331.5M -> 320.3M (-3.4%, I predicted 3-6%), MFU 38.5% -> 37.2%, peak VRAM 32.1 -> 33.0 GB. So 25M extra parameters were bought for only 3% of the token budget and still lost. That means embedding-table capacity is not merely at its optimum, it is past it: the alternating VE pattern is load-bearing, not an arbitrary default, and layer 0 having no VE is apparently fine. Plausible mechanism is that a per-layer value embedding is a shortcut from token identity straight into the value stream, and giving every layer one lets the model lean on token-local information instead of composing across depth. Consistent with the value-residual literature, where VE is applied to a few layers rather than all. This closes the FLOP-free-capacity hypothesis in the direction of MORE; the untested direction is FEWER (e.g. VE on the first two layers plus the last), which would also RAISE token count and is the only remaining cheap probe on this axis.
